review.reason: Candidate 14 is the strongest balanced round. The numbered geometry shows a compact irregular shared property, folded routing with varied orientations, G1 near T2 and G2 near T3, selective groves with grassy breaks, and continuous interior grass. Hole 1 is a 220-yard long par 3 with a substantial target and greenside bunkering; it offers a controlled center-green option against a more exacting pin attack. Hole 2 is a 400-yard cape par 4 with a substantial shoreline and fairway and greenside bunkers, creating a meaningful choice between a safer line and more assertive positioning. Hole 3 is a 573-yard par 5 with a long lake beside the route and multiple bunkers, giving staged placement real consequences while retaining playable landing space. The par-3/4/5 sequence and contrasting hazard patterns make for excellent within-round variety. Long par 3s, cape holes, and water-lined par 5s have appeared recently, so novelty is not exceptional, but the combination and routing distinguish this set sufficiently. Simulated safe tee options of 52/62/48 support fair difficulty, and the previews show credible landing corridors. No geometry correction is needed.
